C1169.title: Bypassing Rate Limits via HTTP/2 Multiplexing and Request Pipelining
C1169.summary: Modern rate limiters often count TCP connections or HTTP/1.1 requests rather than HTTP/2 streams. Attackers can multiplex hundreds of parallel streams over a single TLS connection, making a flood of requests appear as just one connection to the rate limiter and thereby evading restrictions. This technique was widely documented between 2023 and 2025.
